flaws.title: Downward reset scans bitmap words past endTick, so taxed zero-for-one swaps run out of gas when no initialized tick lies below the start
flaws.sequence:
1. A pool's current tick is below every initialized tick. This happens when all liquidity sits above the price, for example after the lowest positions are removed or after a swap pushes the price through all the liquidity.
2. In a new block, a user sends a zero-for-one swap with a non-zero priority fee, so taxInEther > 0 and this is the top-of-block swap.
3. afterSwap calls _zeroForOneDistributeTax, which calls initDown and then reset(startTick) with endTick < startTick.
4. reset finds no set bit at or below startTick in the current word. It then keeps decrementing wordPos and calling getPoolBitmapInfo.
5. The loop only stops at a set bit or at wordPos == type(int16).min. It never checks whether the word already lies entirely below self.endTick.
6. With no initialized ticks below, it scans about 29,000 to 32,700 words, each an external extsload of a cold slot. The hook calls reset a second time later in the same function, doubling the cost.
7. The cost goes far beyond the block gas limit, so afterSwap and the whole swap revert.
flaws.impact: While the price is below the lowest initialized tick, no taxed (top-of-block) zero-for-one swap can execute. Users are blocked from trading in that direction and protocol tax revenue is lost. Gas cost also grows without bound whenever the next initialized tick is far below endTick.

requirement_breaks: The walk is not limited to the range from startTick down to endTick. reset keeps loading bitmap words below endTick until it finds an initialized tick or reaches type(int16).min.
